text:
alex: Quick summary from this morning's novum14b bring-up (int4 quant): long-form summarization evals show consistent quality dip vs f16 baseline. Not huge but reproducible: ROUGE-L -1.8, BLEU -0.9, and a small increase in hallucination rate on set-L.
marie: ack. is this across all seeds / prompts or a narrow subset?
alex: ran 3 seeds across 600 samples each. Failure modes cluster on prompts requiring multi-paragraph coherence and long context (~3.5k tokens). Shorter prompts look identical.
sam: sounds like quantization noise accumulating over long generation window. Did you compare int6 / hybrid quant to see delta?
alex: yes -- quick matrix below (avg over suite-L):
- f16 (baseline): p50 lat 190ms, p95 430ms, cost idx=1.0, rougeL=44.2
- int6 hybrid: p50 160ms, p95 390ms, cost idx=0.78, rougeL=43.9
- int4 (current): p50 140ms, p95 360ms, cost idx=0.62, rougeL=42.4
Note: int4 gives best cost/latency but drops ~1.5-1.8 ROUGE-L vs baseline on long-form.
jia: not surprising. Two mitigation paths: a) per-layer quant fallback for last N layers (reduce quant aggressiveness near output) b) tune runtime defaults (smaller max_new_tokens, different batching) to avoid long per-request state that amplifies quant error.
alex: reproduced one more interesting ops-level behavior: when prefetch_slots >= 96 and adaptive or fixed-window batching >10ms we saw memory churn (slab fragmentation) during warmstart with many long sessions. Logs: ```
[2026-03-24T08:12:03Z] slab_alloc: total=32.0GB used=29.3GB frag=22%
[2026-03-24T08:12:04Z] kv_prefetch: slots=96 in_flight=12
[2026-03-24T08:12:04Z] oom_warn: attempted_alloc=1.9GB free=1.2GB
```
So prefetched KV + long KV caches seem to increase fragmentation which can cause OOMs under concurrent long gens.
marie: got it. For onboarding we should pick safe defaults that balance cost/quality: keep int4 but reduce max_new_tokens default and lower prefetch aggressiveness. Also include a recommended eval checklist for long-generation suites.
sam: proposal: model-catalog profile novum14b-int4-v0.1 defaults -> max_new_tokens=600, batching window_ms=8, prefetch_slots=48, kv_eviction_secs=45, soft-layer-fallback=layers[-4:]. Also add a gating rule: for requests >700 tokens route to int6-hybrid.
qa-bot: quick smoke run enqueued: ./evals/run.py --model novum14b-int4 --suite long-summ --max_new_tokens 600 --batch_window 8 --prefetch_slots 48 --out /tmp/novum-int4-smoke.json
alex: added reproducer in repo: evals/novum14b/repro-longgen/README.md with the above command + dataset snapshot.
jia: can we get a small quality comparison matrix from the evals job before we finalize defaults? would like to see metric deltas on set-S, set-M, set-L.
alex: scheduled. Preliminary numbers indicate ROUGE-L delta vs f16 on set-L drops to -0.8 with those defaults (much improved) while p95 latency increases ~10-12ms vs int4 base. cost still ~0.68 of f16.
marie: that's acceptable tradeoff. Action items:
- alex: finish 2h smoke with synthetic long-gen traffic and attach memory/frag traces (ETA 3h)
- sam: run per-layer int6 fallback experiment (layers -2/-4) and report quality+latency (ETA EOD)
- infra-bot: roll a canary profile novum14b-int4-v0.1 to canary pool (3 nodes) with lower prefetch config when alex signals green
- jia: draft catalog entry + eval checklist PR
infra-bot: canary request queued (ticket #CI-2319)
deploy-bot: canary pool ready when requested :thumbsup:
alex: last note: if per-layer fallback doesn't close gap we should consider shipping int6-hybrid as default for the long-gen tier. For now we add soft-routing and profile.
marie: thanks all. small doc to add to model-catalog: novum14b-int4-v0.1 (defaults + known regressions + eval links). Please keep thread updated with the smoke traces. :sparkles:
